gen-dafont-gobold-gf-noto-serif-khojki: Gobold stretches its letters wide, with curves that never quite close and strokes like a bent paperclip. Noto Serif Khojki does the opposite job, with big bowls and soft shifts in thickness.
gen-dafont-gobold-gf-noto-serif-lao: Flat, wide and fineliner-sharp. Gobold lays down one uniform line, while Noto Serif Lao answers with a bookish lowercase whose thick and thin strokes feel like close relatives.
gen-dafont-gobold-gf-noto-serif-makasar: Gobold's arms and legs keep a constant width, never thinning anywhere. Noto Serif Makasar brings a towering lowercase and hairlines sturdy enough to hold their own beside the stems.
gen-dafont-gobold-gf-noto-serif-malayala: Noto Serif Malayalam has big open counters in every small letter, and its bowls thin gently rather than sharply. Gobold sits above it like glass tubing bent into letters, wide and unhurried.
gen-dafont-gobold-gf-noto-serif-np-hmong: Wide, bold and unbroken. Gobold draws a constant-width pen line, while Noto Serif NP Hmong adds a faint pressure shadow and lowercase bodies that climb close to cap height.
gen-dafont-gobold-gf-noto-serif-old-uygh: Authoritative yet unhurried, Gobold keeps one unvarying weight from word to word, with its curves left open. Noto Serif Old Uyghur adds tall, bulb-like bowls and thins that never turn spindly.
gen-dafont-gobold-gf-noto-serif-oriya: Noto Serif Oriya has curves a touch heavier than its joins, and its lowercase rises almost to capital height. Gobold runs uninterrupted monoline strokes, and the text serif below feels dignified beside it.
gen-dafont-gobold-gf-noto-serif-ottoman-: Gobold draws its letters with the plain line of a fixed-width stencil brush, spread far apart. Noto Serif Ottoman Siyaq has a sizable lowercase and bowls that swell only slightly at their widest.
gen-dafont-gobold-gf-noto-serif-sinhala: Gobold spaces its letters wide, with short ascenders and open curves. Noto Serif Sinhala sits in a tall band of lowercase, its stroke weights differing just enough to keep the serif text alive.
gen-dafont-gobold-gf-noto-serif-telugu: Noto Serif Telugu reads traditionally, with a gentle thick to thin shift and a tall lowercase that nearly reaches the capitals. Yet Gobold's cord-like curves, as heavy as its stems, give the pair its strongest quality: a pointed difference.
